section_title: Human Evidence: Postmortem Pathology, Single-Nucleus Atlases, and CSF Somatostatin as a Biomarker
thesis: The human evidence contains the strongest and the weakest claims in this review. Four independent single-nucleus and deconvolution cohorts converge on depletion of SST inhibitory neurons in Alzheimer cortex, early along the pathological trajectory, by a method that does not depend on peptide detection. CSF somatostatin, by contrast, is reduced in Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, frontotemporal dementia and late-life depression alike, is modified by medication, has never been reported with a sensitivity, specificity or AUC, and is reversible after shunting - it is not a biomarker of interneuron loss.
scope_notes: Human evidence synthesis: postmortem, snRNA-seq atlases, CSF SST biomarker performance.

findings.effect_size: qualitative: lowered SST-14 with significant increase in unprocessed 15 kDa precursor
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: It was observed that the patients have a lowered content in the tetradecapeptide somatostatin while they exhibit a significant increase in unprocessed 15 Kda precursor.
findings.study_system: human CSF from Alzheimer's disease patients; radioimmunoassay of SST-14, SST-28 and 15 kDa prosomatostatin

findings.claim: CSF somatostatin reduction in AD scales with cortical dysfunction measured independently: it correlates with intellectual impairment and with PET glucose hypometabolism, most closely in parietal cortex, where postmortem tissue SST is also selectively reduced.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Somatostatin-like immunoreactivity in Alzheimer CSF was significantly lower than in that from age-matched controls.
findings.evidence: Triangulates the same biochemical deficit across three measurement domains (CSF, functional imaging, postmortem tissue) within one study, including a regional dissociation (parietal versus frontal).
findings.effect_size: qualitative: close association between CSF somatostatin reduction and parietal glucose hypometabolism; postmortem SST lower in posterior parietal but not anterior frontal cortex
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In postmortem cortical tissue from Alzheimer patients, somatostatin levels were lower in posterior parietal but not in anterior frontal cortex.
findings.study_system: human CSF plus FDG-PET in Alzheimer's disease and age-matched controls, with postmortem cortical tissue somatostatin measurements

findings.claim: Low CSF somatostatin is shared by Alzheimer's disease and late-life depression, so the reduction is not diagnostically specific; the association with cognition holds across the pooled sample but not within diagnostic groups.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Patients with dementia or depression were found to have lower CSF somatostatin concentrations than control subjects despite markedly different clinical presentations.
findings.evidence: Includes a psychiatric comparison group rather than only healthy controls, which is the design that exposes the specificity problem; also shows depression severity does not track somatostatin.
findings.effect_size: significant positive correlation between CSF SST-like immunoreactivity and cognitive functioning across all 47 subjects, not significant within individual diagnostic groups
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: There was a significant positive correlation between CSF somatostatin-like immunoreactivity and cognitive functioning in all 47 subjects, but this association was not statistically significant within individual diagnostic groups.
findings.study_system: human CSF from 12 Alzheimer's disease patients, 15 age-matched controls and 20 older depressed subjects

findings.claim: In a memory-clinic population, CSF somatostatin correlates with CSF amyloid-beta 1-42 rather than with tau, and is confounded by vascular and metabolic factors including hypertension, diabetes and cholesterol levels.
findings.claim_source_sentence: CSF SOM concentrations remained independently associated with CSF Aβ1–42 concentrations (p = 0.01) and blood total cholesterol concentrations (p = 0.03) and CSF NPY remained significantly associated with CSF T-Tau (p = 0.03).
findings.evidence: Multivariable adjustment identifies systemic confounders of the CSF somatostatin signal, a pre-analytical/clinical confound rarely addressed in the earlier RIA literature; the authors note the population is small.
findings.effect_size: CSF SOM independently associated with CSF Abeta1-42 (p = 0.01) and blood total cholesterol (p = 0.03); univariate associates of high CSF SOM included hypertension (p = 0.004) and diabetes (p < 0.0001)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Factors associated with high CSF SOM concentrations were hypertension (p = 0.004), diabetes (p < 0.0001), low plasma total cholesterol (p = 0.004) and LDL cholesterol (p = 0.002), high CSF NPY concentrations (p = 0.03) and high CSF Aβ1–42 concentrations (p = 0.03; Table 2).
findings.study_system: human lumbar CSF from a memory-clinic cohort with paired core AD biomarkers (Abeta1-42, T-tau, P-tau), somatostatin and NPY, plus vascular and metabolic covariates

findings.claim: CSF somatostatin reduction can be reversible and is not a fixed marker of neuronal loss: shunting in normal pressure hydrocephalus significantly increased CSF somatostatin in all patients, yet cognitive performance did not improve.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Results After shunting, SOM and CRF concentrations were significantly increased in all patients.
findings.evidence: Within-subject intervention design with a biochemical and a clinical endpoint; dissociates CSF peptide concentration from cognitive outcome, which argues the CSF measure partly indexes CSF dynamics rather than interneuron integrity.
findings.effect_size: SOM and CRF concentrations significantly increased in all patients; NPY increased in 12 of 14; clinical condition improved in 13 of 14 but no significant neuropsychological change
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Concentrations of NPY were increased in 12 of the 14 patients studied.
findings.study_system: human lumbar CSF from 14 normal pressure hydrocephalus patients before and 6-9 months after shunt surgery, with neuropsychological and functional assessment

findings.claim: In AD frontal cortex, somatostatin- and NPY-positive neurons are reduced by more than 70% with a concomitant astrocytic increase, while SSTR2 and SSTR4 remain the predominant receptor subtypes.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In AD cortical brain region, somatostatin and neuropeptide-Y-positive neurons decreased (>70%), and glial fibrillary acidic protein-positive astrocytes significantly increased (>130%) in comparison to control brain.
findings.evidence: Reports ligand-expressing neurons and all five receptor subtypes in the same cases, so ligand loss can be separated from receptor availability; the >70% neuron loss is far larger than most other cortical estimates and NPY loss here contradicts earlier NPY-sparing reports.
findings.effect_size: somatostatin- and NPY-positive neurons decreased >70%; GFAP-positive astrocytes increased >130% versus control
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In AD cortical brain region, somatostatin and neuropeptide-Y-positive neurons decreased (>70%), and glial fibrillary acidic protein-positive astrocytes significantly increased (>130%) in comparison to control brain.
findings.study_system: human postmortem frontal cortex, AD versus age-matched controls; immunohistochemistry for SSTR1-5 antigens plus SST, NPY and GFAP

findings.claim: Common variation in the somatostatin gene modifies AD risk and interacts with APOE genotype, providing genetic support for somatostatinergic involvement upstream of the pathology.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In the whole study group, the age, sex and APOE adjusted OR for the risk of AD in C-allele carriers of the SNP rs4988 514 was 1.42 (p <0.05).
findings.evidence: Case-control genetic design with covariate adjustment and a prespecified candidate locus adjacent to a previously identified Finnish late-onset AD linkage region; no independent replication cohort was identified in these searches.
findings.effect_size: age, sex and APOE adjusted OR 1.42 (p < 0.05) for rs4988514 C-allele carriers; OR rises to 2.05 (p < 0.01) within APOE epsilon-4 carriers
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Interestingly, in APOE epsilon4-allele carriers, the age and sex adjusted OR for the risk of AD in C-allele carriers of the rs4988 514 increased to 2.05 (p <0.01).
findings.study_system: Finnish case-control genetic association study, 424 AD patients and 466 non-demented controls, three SNPs in the somatostatin gene

findings.claim: In the Parkinson's disease amygdala, somatostatin-expressing neurons are largely spared from alpha-synuclein co-aggregation whereas parvalbumin-expressing neurons are frequently affected, an inversion of the interneuron vulnerability hierarchy reported in AD cortex.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Parvalbumin-positive cells colocalized frequently with α-synuclein (68.44%), whereas, somatostatin-positive cells colocalized only occasionally (6.98%).
findings.evidence: Direct within-tissue comparison of two interneuron markers against the same pathological inclusion, so the contrast is internally controlled; small n (5 per group).
findings.effect_size: parvalbumin-positive cells colocalised with alpha-synuclein in 68.44% of cases versus 6.98% for somatostatin-positive cells
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Parvalbumin-positive cells colocalized frequently with α-synuclein (68.44%), whereas, somatostatin-positive cells colocalized only occasionally (6.98%).
findings.study_system: human postmortem basolateral, central and cortical amygdaloid nuclei from 5 PD patients (Braak stages 3-5) and 5 controls; alpha-synuclein co-localisation immunohistochemistry

findings.claim: A negative mechanistic result: although PC2 is required for prosomatostatin cleavage, the mature PC2 enzyme pool and its activity are unchanged in AD frontal cortex, so convertase failure does not explain the cortical somatostatin deficit.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, the content and enzymatic activity of the PC2 mature form were similar in Alzheimer patients and controls.
findings.evidence: Directly tests the processing hypothesis raised by CSF precursor studies and rejects it for cortex; also asserts the deficit occurs without major loss of SST-containing neurons, which conflicts with the cell-count literature.
findings.effect_size: marked decrease in the ratio of PC2 precursor to total enzymatic pool in AD frontal cortex, coinciding with increased binding protein 7B2, but no change in PC1
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In contrast, a marked decrease in the ratio of the PC2 precursor to the total enzymatic pool was observed in the frontal cortex of Alzheimer patients.
findings.study_system: human postmortem frontal and temporal cortex (AD versus control) with PC2-null mouse cortex as the mechanistic reference; size exclusion chromatography, immunohistochemistry, western blot and enzyme activity assay

findings.claim: Single-nucleus analysis across AD stages finds a significant group difference in Sst neuron numbers overall, but no significant difference in Sst or Sst Chodl proportions in the smaller stage-wise comparison, showing the depletion signal is sensitive to cohort size and normalisation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: (c) Sst, One-way ANOVA revealed a significant difference between groups (F(3,81) = 4.381, p = 0.0066). **p < 0.01, vs Controls; Tukey's test.
findings.evidence: Reports both significant and null tests on the same cell class from the same data, which exposes how the SST depletion result depends on the statistical unit (absolute number versus proportion) and on group sizes.
findings.effect_size: Sst neuron number differed between donor categories (one-way ANOVA F(3,81) = 4.381, p = 0.0066); in the separate comparison Sst showed no significant difference (t(6) = 1.333, p = 0.2309) nor did Sst Chodl (t(6) = 0.8563, p = 0.4247)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: (c) Sst, there is no significant difference between groups (t-test, t(6) = 1.333, p = 0.2309).
findings.study_system: human postmortem cortex single-nucleus transcriptomic data grouped by AD stage, cell-type-level neuron counts and proportions

findings.claim: A polygenic score built to index SST-expressing interneuron function was applied to a late-life cohort to test whether genetically indexed SST+ cell function predicts depressive symptoms and cognitive performance in ageing.
findings.claim_source_sentence: For individuals with SST-PRSs, 2 groups were created: those with cognitive data (n = 473; aged 67.33 ± 4.34 years; 48% female) and those with complete Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) data (n = 272; age 69.63 ± 6.01 years; 76% female).
findings.evidence: Translates the postmortem SST-cell-loss literature into a genetically indexed, antemortem measure; the cohort is a late-life depression trial rather than a neurodegenerative cohort, so transfer to AD is untested.
findings.effect_size: SST-PRS cohort: 473 participants with cognitive data (aged 67.33 +/- 4.34 years, 48% female) and 272 with complete PHQ-9 data
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: For individuals with SST-PRSs, 2 groups were created: those with cognitive data (n = 473; aged 67.33 ± 4.34 years; 48% female) and those with complete Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) data (n = 272; age 69.63 ± 6.01 years; 76% female).
findings.study_system: human genotype and clinical data from a late-life depression trial cohort, with an SST-expressing-interneuron-derived polygenic risk score built from eQTL and expression data

findings.claim: In Alzheimer-type dementia, CSF cholinesterase activity and somatostatin-like immunoreactivity appear to track dementia severity
findings.claim_source_sentence: In the AD/SDAT patients cholinesterase and somatostatin-like immunoreactivity levels seemed to be correlated with the severity of dementia.
findings.evidence: CSF cholinesterase and somatostatin-like immunoreactivity measured in 59 patients with dementia of the Alzheimer type and 19 age-matched non-demented controls
findings.effect_size: Qualitative: SLI levels correlated with severity of dementia (no coefficient reported)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Cholinesterase (ChE) activity and somatostatin-like immunoreactivity (SLI) of the cerebrospinal fluid were determined for 59 patients with dementia of the Alzheimer type (AD/SDAT) and for 19 age-matched control patients with no signs of dementia.
findings.study_system: human lumbar CSF, Alzheimer-type dementia (n=59) and age-matched controls (n=19)

findings.claim: The same study documents parallel cortical and CSF somatostatin deficits in Alzheimer's disease, with regionally graded cortical reductions
findings.claim_source_sentence: In the CSF among 75 AD patients SLI was 35% lower (P less than 0.001) than in controls.
findings.evidence: Radioimmunoassay of somatostatin-like immunoreactivity in postmortem cortex (6 AD vs 11 controls) and in CSF of 75 AD patients
findings.effect_size: CSF SLI 35% lower than controls (P<0.001); cortical SLI decreased 42% frontal (P<0.005), 28% temporal (P<0.05), 42% parietal (P<0.01), unchanged in thalamus and putamen
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In 6 AD patients the SLI values were decreased 42% (P less than 0.005) in the frontal cortex, 28% (P less than 0.05) in the temporal cortex and 42% (P less than 0.01) in the parietal cortex but not in the thalamus and putamen compared to 11 control patients.
findings.study_system: human postmortem cortex and lumbar CSF, Alzheimer's disease

findings.claim: Although CSF somatostatin is reduced in Alzheimer's disease and multi-infarct dementia, values overlap controls so heavily that the measure has no diagnostic specificity
findings.claim_source_sentence: Concentrations of SLI in AD patients overlapped those in both normal subjects and patients with multi-infarct dementia, so that changes in CSF SLI have no diagnostic specificity.
findings.evidence: CSF SLI radioimmunoassay across AD, multi-infarct dementia, normal-pressure hydrocephalus, Parkinson's and Huntington's disease with chromatographic characterisation
findings.effect_size: Reduced in AD and multi-infarct dementia (p<0.01) but not in NPH, Parkinson's or Huntington's disease; distributions overlap controls
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Concentrations of somatostatin-like immunoreactivity (SLI) in CSF were reduced in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and multi-infarct dementia (p less than 0.01), but not in normal-pressure hydrocephalus, Parkinson's disease, and Huntington's disease.
findings.study_system: human lumbar CSF across multiple neurological diagnoses

findings.claim: CSF somatostatin is pharmacologically modifiable and tracks cognitive response: cholinesterase-inhibitor responders show rising CSF-SLI while non-responders decline
findings.claim_source_sentence: The CSF-SLI increased significantly (P = 0.01) in the responders for the treatment (increase of the Mini-Mental State Examination score greater than or equal to 3; n = 11), while the non-responders (n = 9) showed a significant decrease of CSF-SLI (P = 0.003).
findings.evidence: Tetrahydroaminoacridine treatment trial in probable Alzheimer's disease with paired CSF-SLI sampling and MMSE response stratification
findings.effect_size: CSF-SLI increased in responders (P=0.01, n=11) and decreased in non-responders (P=0.003, n=9); change correlated with neuropsychological performance (P=0.001)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The CSF-SLI increased significantly (P = 0.01) in the responders for the treatment (increase of the Mini-Mental State Examination score greater than or equal to 3; n = 11), while the non-responders (n = 9) showed a significant decrease of CSF-SLI (P = 0.003).
findings.study_system: human lumbar CSF, probable Alzheimer's disease under tetrahydroaminoacridine treatment

findings.claim: In untreated early parkinsonian syndrome CSF somatostatin is increased rather than decreased, directly opposing the deficit reported in established Parkinson's disease
findings.claim_source_sentence: These results indicate that in the early steps of untreated parkinsonian syndrome, somatostatin concentration in cerebrospinal fluid may increase, probably due to the neurodegenerative depletion of somatostatin from striatal or cortical neurons.
findings.evidence: CSF SLI radioimmunoassay in 23 patients with untreated parkinsonian syndrome (15 idiopathic Parkinson's disease) with memory testing
findings.effect_size: Significant increase in CSF somatostatin in idiopathic Parkinson's disease patients with severe memory impairment
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: A test of learning memory was used to evaluate the mental state of patients and a significant increase in CSF-somatostatin levels was observed in patients with Idiopathic Parkinson's disease and severe affectation of memory.
findings.study_system: human lumbar CSF, untreated early parkinsonian syndrome

findings.claim: Mean CSF somatostatin is roughly halved in Alzheimer's disease relative to other neurological patients, with a threshold separating dementia cases
findings.claim_source_sentence: The AD patients had significantly lower mean CSF somatostatin than the "other" neurological patients (14.6 +/- 1.5 S.E.M. versus 26.7 +/- 3.2 pg/ml, p less than 0.005).
findings.evidence: CSF somatostatin radioimmunoassay comparing AD and Parkinson's-disease dementia with other neurological patients
findings.effect_size: 14.6 +/- 1.5 pg/ml (AD) versus 26.7 +/- 3.2 pg/ml (other neurological patients), p<0.005
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The AD patients had significantly lower mean CSF somatostatin than the "other" neurological patients (14.6 +/- 1.5 S.E.M. versus 26.7 +/- 3.2 pg/ml, p less than 0.005).
findings.study_system: human lumbar CSF, Alzheimer's disease versus other neurological disease

findings.claim: CSF somatostatin is markedly reduced not only in manifest Huntington's disease but also in symptom-free offspring, suggesting a presymptomatic somatostatinergic change
findings.claim_source_sentence: Substance P levels were not significantly altered, but somatostatin levels were markedly decreased both in affected patients and symptom-free offspring.
findings.evidence: CSF somatostatin, substance P and cyclic nucleotide measurements in Huntington's disease patients, first-generation relatives and neurological controls
findings.effect_size: Qualitative: markedly decreased somatostatin in both affected patients and symptom-free offspring; substance P unaltered
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Substance P levels were not significantly altered, but somatostatin levels were markedly decreased both in affected patients and symptom-free offspring.
findings.study_system: human lumbar CSF, Huntington's disease patients and at-risk offspring

findings.claim: A discordant CSF series finds only a slight somatostatin reduction in presenile Alzheimer's disease and no reduction at all in senile-onset cases
findings.claim_source_sentence: The mean concentration of SLI was only slightly reduced in patients with AD in the presenium compared to control, and was unaltered from control in the examples of AD of senile age.
findings.evidence: Lumbar CSF SLI radioimmunoassay in clinically suspected Alzheimer's disease of presenile and senile onset versus controls aged 22-73
findings.effect_size: Only slight reduction in presenile AD; unaltered from control in senile-onset AD
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The mean concentration of SLI was only slightly reduced in patients with AD in the presenium compared to control, and was unaltered from control in the examples of AD of senile age.
findings.study_system: human lumbar CSF, presenile and senile-onset Alzheimer's disease

findings.claim: Mass-spectrometric peptide profiling shows that radioimmunoassay-based CSF somatostatin deficits may reflect altered peptide processing and fragment detection rather than lower peptide output
findings.claim_source_sentence: The majority of studies of neuropeptides in CSF have not been verified by HPLC. The observed decrease in a neuropeptide level as measured by RIA may therefore reflect an altered synthesis or extracellular processing, resulting in neuropeptide fragments that may or may not be detected by RIA. Matrix-assisted laser desorption time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-MS) has been shown to be a powerful technique in the analysis of biological materials without any pre-treatment, by detecting peptides and proteins at a specific mass-to-charge (m/z) ratio.
findings.evidence: MALDI mass spectrometry of neuropeptide processing in CSF from AD (n=3), FTD (n=3) and controls (n=2), compared against the RIA literature
findings.effect_size: Qualitative: considerable inter-individual variability in CSF neuropeptide metabolism rate and in the number of peptide fragments generated
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We studied the processing of the neuropeptides NPY, NPY, SOM and GAL in the cerebrospinal fluid of patients with AD (n = 3), FTD (n = 3) and controls (n = 2) using MALDI-MS. We found that considerable inter-individual variability exists in the rate of neuropeptide metabolism in CSF, as well as the number of peptide fragments formed.
findings.study_system: human lumbar CSF, Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia and controls (MALDI-MS)

findings.claim: Somatostatin-28 degradation kinetics are themselves altered in Alzheimer-type dementia cortex, so measured peptide levels confound synthesis with catabolism
findings.claim_source_sentence: The metabolic half-life of SS-28 was significantly reduced in post-mortem Brodmann Area 22 of SDAT tissue.
findings.evidence: Regional measurement of somatostatin-28 metabolic half-life and peptidase activity in postmortem SDAT and control brain tissue
findings.effect_size: Significantly reduced SS-28 metabolic half-life in postmortem Brodmann Area 22 of SDAT tissue
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The metabolic half-life of SS-28 was significantly reduced in post-mortem Brodmann Area 22 of SDAT tissue.
findings.study_system: human postmortem cortex (Brodmann area 22), senile dementia of the Alzheimer type

findings.claim: CSF somatostatin is reduced to a similar degree in Binswanger's disease and in severe Alzheimer-type dementia, but correlates with dementia score only in the Alzheimer group
findings.claim_source_sentence: Levels of SLI were significantly decreased in BD in general and in SDAT patients with severe dementia (GDS 7), compared to a control group (BD overall 19.7 +/- 11.6 fmol/ml, SDAT 18.6 +/- 7.9 vs. 30.5 +/- 8.6 fmol/ml in controls, p < 0.01 for both).
findings.evidence: CSF SLI and monoamine metabolite measurement in 21 Binswanger's disease and 53 Alzheimer's disease patients versus controls
findings.effect_size: SLI 19.7 +/- 11.6 fmol/ml (Binswanger) and 18.6 +/- 7.9 fmol/ml (severe SDAT) versus 30.5 +/- 8.6 fmol/ml in controls (p<0.01); SLI-dementia score correlation r=-0.65, p<0.05 in SDAT only
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In SDAT patients, SLI levels correlated with dementia scores (r = -0.65, p < 0.05), but not in BD. HVA levels were decreased significantly in SDAT and BD patients with severe dementia (SDAT 273.5 +/- 138.7, BD 224.3 +/- 69.9 vs. 364.9 +/- 103.8 nmol/ml, p < 0.01 in controls, p < 0.05 for both).
findings.study_system: human lumbar CSF, Binswanger's disease and Alzheimer's disease

findings.claim: Two prosomatostatin-derived peptides fall in parallel in Alzheimer's cortex, arguing that the deficit reflects loss of somatostatin neurons rather than a shift in post-translational processing
findings.claim_source_sentence: The similar reductions of two prosomatostatin-derived peptides in AD cerebral cortex supports the contention that decreased somatostatin immunoreactivity in AD is caused by a degeneration of somatostatin cortical neurons and terminals.
findings.evidence: Radioimmunoassay of somatostatin-28(1-12)-like and somatostatin-14-like immunoreactivity in matched Alzheimer's disease cortical regions
findings.effect_size: Regional SOM-28(1-12) reductions significantly correlated with somatostatin-14-like immunoreactivity decreases in the same regions
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Reductions were significantly correlated with decreases in somatostatin-14-like immunoreactivity in the same regions.
findings.study_system: human postmortem cerebral cortex, Alzheimer's disease

findings.claim: In Huntington's disease striatum somatostatin-28(1-12) immunoreactivity is increased rather than depleted, while cortical areas are unchanged
findings.claim_source_sentence: Concentrations of immunoreactive somatostatin-28(1-12) were significantly increased in the caudate and putamen but were unchanged in cortical areas A9 and A17.
findings.evidence: Specific radioimmunoassay of somatostatin-28(1-12) in Huntington's disease postmortem caudate, putamen and cortical areas
findings.effect_size: Significantly increased in caudate and putamen; unchanged in cortical areas A9 and A17
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Concentrations of immunoreactive somatostatin-28(1-12) were significantly increased in the caudate and putamen but were unchanged in cortical areas A9 and A17.
findings.study_system: human postmortem striatum and cortex, Huntington's disease

findings.claim: Somatostatin receptor binding, not only the peptide itself, is reduced in Alzheimer's disease cortex, and the loss is regionally selective
findings.claim_source_sentence: In the frontal cortex (Brodmann areas 6, 9, and 10) and temporal cortex (Brodmann area 21), the concentrations of somatostatin in receptors in the patients were reduced to approximately 50 percent of control values.
findings.evidence: Receptor binding assay of somatostatin receptors across multiple Brodmann areas in Alzheimer's disease and control postmortem brain
findings.effect_size: Receptor concentrations reduced to approximately 50% of control in frontal (BA 6, 9, 10) and temporal (BA 21) cortex; 40% reduction in hippocampus; no change in cingulate cortex, postcentral gyrus, temporal pole or superior temporal gyrus
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: A 40 percent reduction was seen in the hippocampus, while no significant changes were found in the cingulate cortex, postcentral gyrus, temporal pole, and superior temporal gyrus.
findings.study_system: human postmortem cortex and hippocampus, Alzheimer's disease

findings.claim: Striatal somatostatin receptor density is markedly reduced in Huntington's chorea, consistent with loss of the postsynaptic neurons that carry these receptors
findings.claim_source_sentence: Marked reductions of the density of somatostatin binding sites were observed in the caudate and putamen of all patients with Huntington's chorea.
findings.evidence: Quantitative receptor autoradiography of striatal somatostatin receptors in 6 Huntington's chorea brains versus 12 neurological controls and 7 schizophrenia cases
findings.effect_size: Marked reductions of somatostatin binding site density in caudate and putamen of all Huntington's chorea patients
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Using quantitative receptor autoradiography we examined the density and distribution of somatostatin receptors in the striatum of 6 patients dying from Huntington's chorea degree 3, in 12 control healthy patients dying without neurological diseases and 7 schizophrenic patients, using the stable somatostatin octapeptide analogue [125I]204-090 as a radioligand.
findings.study_system: human postmortem striatum, Huntington's chorea (grade 3)

findings.claim: A split morphometric result: with atrophy correction, somatostatin-immunoreactive FIBRE LENGTH per cortical strip did not differ significantly between control and Alzheimer's disease frontal or temporal cortex, whereas somatostatin-immunoreactive PERIKARYA were significantly fewer in Alzheimer's disease in temporal cortex layers II + III combined
findings.claim_source_sentence: Using a randomized method to quantify immunostained fibre length in the neuropil, an analysis of variance revealed no significant differences in the mean SLI or NPYLI fibre length per cortical strip between control and AD groups in frontal or temporal cortex.
findings.evidence: Immunocytochemical quantification of SLI and NPY-LI perikarya and fibre length with atrophy correction in 6 control and 6 AD frontal and temporal cortices
findings.effect_size: No significant difference in mean SLI or NPY-LI fibre length per cortical strip between control and AD in frontal or temporal cortex
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: This study reports the numbers of somatostatin-like (SLI) and neuropeptide Y-like immunoreactive (NPYLI) neuronal perikarya and the length of SLI and NPYLI immunoreactive fibres, with appropriate corrections for atrophy in 6 control and 6 AD cases.
findings.study_system: human postmortem frontal and temporal cortex, Alzheimer's disease (immunocytochemistry with atrophy correction)
findings.claim_source_sentence_perikarya: There were significantly fewer SLI neurones in AD in layers II + III combined from the temporal cortex, and fewer NPYLI neurones in layers V + VI in both frontal and temporal cortices.
findings.correction_note: COORDINATOR CORRECTION (pre-assembly). The previous claim field read: "A morphometric negative result: somatostatin-immunoreactive perikaryal numbers and fibre length are not significantly reduced in Alzheimer's disease cortex once atrophy is corrected for". That wrongly extended the paper's fibre-length null to its perikaryal counts; the claim_source_sentence it cites speaks only of fibre length, and the abstract reports the opposite for perikarya. The round-3 blinded figure audit independently caught the same inversion and reversed it in the section 09 figure plan, and the section 09 prose was already correct and verbatim-sourced. Only the claim field and argument_role were stale. No numeral was added: both directions are now carried by their own verbatim source sentences.

findings.claim: In a large postmortem series the cortical somatostatin deficit is near-global across cortical regions while neuropeptide Y is entirely spared, establishing selectivity among neuropeptide-defined interneurons
findings.claim_source_sentence: Concentrations of SLI were lower in AD patients relative to controls in 9 of 10 cortical regions.
findings.evidence: Radioimmunoassay of SLI and NPY-LI in 10 cortical regions from 49 Alzheimer's disease patients and 9 elderly controls
findings.effect_size: SLI lower in 9 of 10 cortical regions; no significant NPY-LI difference in any of 10 regions
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In contrast, no significant differences in NPYLI concentrations between the two groups were observed in any of 10 regions.
findings.study_system: human postmortem cerebral cortex (10 regions), Alzheimer's disease

findings.claim: In olivopontocerebellar atrophy cortical somatostatin is reduced in a regional pattern unlike Alzheimer's disease, and the reduction dissociates from the cholinergic deficit
findings.claim_source_sentence: Mean concentrations of SLI in OPCA were significantly reduced by 42-58% in parietal and occipital cortices and frontal cortical eye fields, but were normal in other cortical areas, including two subdivisions of the temporal cortex which show marked depletions of both SLI and ChAT in Alzheimer's disease.
findings.evidence: Regional radioimmunoassay of SLI and choline acetyltransferase in OPCA postmortem cortex compared with Alzheimer's disease patterns
findings.effect_size: SLI reduced by 42-58% in parietal and occipital cortices and frontal cortical eye fields, normal in other cortical areas including two temporal subdivisions
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Mean concentrations of SLI in OPCA were significantly reduced by 42-58% in parietal and occipital cortices and frontal cortical eye fields, but were normal in other cortical areas, including two subdivisions of the temporal cortex which show marked depletions of both SLI and ChAT in Alzheimer's disease.
findings.study_system: human postmortem cerebral cortex, olivopontocerebellar atrophy

findings.claim: In the Alzheimer temporal lobe somatostatin, cortistatin and their receptors are reduced while neprilysin expression is unchanged, implying the amyloid-degradation defect lies upstream of neprilysin transcription
findings.claim_source_sentence: Conversely, neprilysin expression was not altered in AD, suggesting that Abeta accumulation observed in AD is due to a lack of neprilysin activation by SST rather than to a reduction of its expression.
findings.evidence: Quantitative real-time PCR of SST/CST, sst1-5, drd1-5 and neprilysin mRNA in three temporal-lobe regions of Alzheimer's disease patients and controls
findings.effect_size: Overall reduction of SST/CST and receptor systems in the temporal lobe; neprilysin expression not altered

arg_conflict_cluster_08_conf_01.thesis: Whether cortical SST-immunoreactive cell density is actually reduced in Alzheimer-type dementia. One study reports 60-80% loss of SST28-IR neuron density in cortical areas 9 and 25; the other reports no decrease in neocortical SST-IR cell density versus aged normals, attributing the pathology instead to swollen, plaque-associated SST fibres. The studies differ in antiserum specificity (SST-28-selective versus generic somatostatin), cortical area sampled, and whether density was formally quantified.

Whether cortical SST-immunoreactive density is reduced at all in Alzheimer-type dementia; antiserum specificity and area sampled differ. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): measurement_modality_and_what_was_counted.

arg_conflict_cluster_08_conf_02.thesis: Whether cortical somatostatin-like immunoreactivity is reduced in AD at all. The first RIA study reports reduced cortical SLI in AD/SDAT; the later study, matching cases and controls for age and postmortem delay and measuring both SLI and [3H]somatostatin binding in areas 9 and 21, finds no significant change in any disease group and concludes somatostatinergic involvement is not a consistent primary feature.

arg_conflict_cluster_08_conf_05.thesis: Method-dependent disagreement on whether the cortical somatostatin deficit reflects loss of somatostatin neurons: tissue radioimmunoassay finds lower SLI in 9 of 10 cortical regions, whereas atrophy-corrected immunocytochemical morphometry in the same disease finds no significant difference in somatostatin-immunoreactive perikaryal number or fibre length. Peptide content per neuron and detectability of lightly stained neurons are the unresolved confounds.

Subgroup composition rather than assay appears to drive the difference.

arg_unanchored.thesis: The human evidence contains the strongest and the weakest claims in this review. Four independent single-nucleus and deconvolution cohorts converge on depletion of SST inhibitory neurons in Alzheimer cortex, early along the pathological trajectory, by a method that does not depend on peptide detection. CSF somatostatin, by contrast, is reduced in Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, frontotemporal dementia and late-life depression alike, is modified by medication, has never been reported with a sensitivity, specificity or AUC, and is reversible after shunting - it is not a biomarker of interneuron loss.

Do not cover them sequentially.

Measured quantity differs: SST-28-selective immunoreactive neuron density, somatostatin mRNA-containing cell density, pan-SST immunoreactive cell counts, and bulk-tissue peptide concentration are not interchangeable.
The APOE-genotype entry compares genotype subgroups within patients, not patients versus controls, so its percent difference is not a disease effect.

Two studies in this cluster report no significant reduction (one for neocortical SST-IR cell density, one for cortical SLI and somatostatin binding) but report no number and are therefore excluded from the plot — their absence biases the plotted distribution towards loss.
Sample sizes are small (5-19 per group) and postmortem delay is matched in only some studies.

Plotting them together makes the heterogeneity, rather than a consensus effect size, the visible result.

The Science 1985 entry measures somatostatin receptor concentration, not peptide concentration, and is not interchangeable with the RIA entries
The PSP entry is a null result entered as 0% and has no reported variance
Diagnoses differ (AD, parkinsonian dementia with AD pathology, OPCA, PSP); the comparison is deliberately cross-disease
All entries are bulk tissue extracts, so none distinguishes neuron loss from reduced peptide content per neuron

(A) Reported deficits span a four-fold range and are measured on incommensurable quantities; two studies reporting no reduction at all give no number and are shown as annotated markers, because omitting them biases the plotted distribution towards loss. Sample sizes are small (5-19 per group) and postmortem delay is matched in only some studies. (B) Bulk-tissue deficits of 28-58% recur in Alzheimer’s disease, Alzheimer-type parkinsonian dementia and olivopontocerebellar atrophy but are absent in progressive supranuclear palsy; the receptor-concentration entry measures a different quantity, and no entry distinguishes neuron loss from reduced peptide content per neuron.

figures.label: fig:sec9-csf-somatostatin-is-not-specific
figures.argument_supported: Supports the review's negative biomarker verdict: CSF somatostatin is reduced across unrelated diagnoses, reported without discrimination statistics, and not comparable between assays.

caveats_to_reproduce_in_caption: Reported metrics are incommensurable: absolute pg/ml concentrations, p-values for group difference, and correlation coefficients with cognition are mixed because most reports give no concentrations.
Diagnoses differ (Parkinson's disease, SDAT, AD, FTD, late-life depression, memory-clinic mixed), so the entries are not replicates of one effect.

Assays differ across four decades: polyclonal radioimmunoassay with varying cross-reactivity to SST-28 and cortistatin, versus a modern immunoassay; only one study reports HPLC molecular-form resolution and only one reports non-cross-reactivity with cortistatin.
Medication is an uncontrolled modifier: neuroleptics raised CSF SLI in one cohort and L-dopa raised the high-molecular-weight form in another.
One study reports total somatostatin plus molecular forms, the others total immunoreactivity only.
data_sources.what_it_reveals_from_evidence: CSF somatostatin is reported low in Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer-type dementia, frontotemporal dementia and late-life depression alike, and in one intervention study rises after shunting without cognitive benefit. The comparison shows the measure lacks diagnostic specificity and that only a minority of studies report an interpretable concentration; the rest report only p-values or correlations, which is itself a reporting problem for any attempted meta-analysis.

caveats_to_reproduce_in_caption: Units are not uniform: two studies report pg/mL, one reports fmol/ml, so values cannot be plotted on a common axis without conversion assumptions
Comparison groups differ: age-matched healthy controls (archneur 1988, Karger 1997) versus 'other neurological patients' (Neurobiol Aging 1984)
Error terms differ (SD vs SEM)
All three use in-house radioimmunoassays with no cross-calibration standard
data_sources.what_it_reveals_from_evidence: Three independent RIA series agree on a 25-45% lower mean CSF somatostatin in dementia, but absolute values are reported in incompatible units (pg/mL vs fmol/ml) against different comparison groups, which is why no diagnostic cut-off has ever transferred between cohorts

figures.what_it_reveals_that_text_cannot: A diagnosis-by-reporting-completeness layout shows both findings at once: the lack of diagnostic specificity, and the fact that most reports provide no concentration at all - a reporting problem that a narrative review would state but could not demonstrate.
figures.plot_plan: Two panels. (A) One row per study grouped by diagnosis (PD, SDAT/AD, FTD, late-life depression, memory-clinic mixed, normal pressure hydrocephalus pre/post shunt), with a column strip encoding what was reported: concentration, p-value only, or correlation only; medication modifiers annotated. (B) The three series reporting absolute concentrations, plotted as ratio to their own comparison group with raw values and units printed, error-term type labelled, and no common axis across units. A margin box states that no retrieved study reports sensitivity, specificity, AUC or a cut-off.
figures.caption_draft: Cerebrospinal fluid somatostatin across diagnoses. (A) Reductions are reported in Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer-type dementia, frontotemporal dementia and late-life depression alike, and most reports give only p-values or correlations rather than concentrations; assays span four decades with uncharacterised cross-reactivity to SST-28 and cortistatin in all but one study, and medication raises the measure in two cohorts. (B) The three series reporting absolute concentrations agree on a 25-45% lower mean in dementia but are expressed in incompatible units against different comparison groups, which is why no diagnostic cut-off has transferred between cohorts. No retrieved study reports a discrimination statistic.

figures.label: fig:sec9-single-nucleus-cohort-convergence
figures.argument_supported: Audits the strongest claim in the review: four human cohorts of different size and design converge on early depletion of SST inhibitory neurons in AD cortex, with identified fragilities.

caveats_to_reproduce_in_caption: Regions differ: dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, middle temporal gyrus plus area 9, six-region panel including thalamus and hippocampus, and frontal cortex.

Cell-type granularity differs: SEA-AD supertypes, ROSMAP subtypes, 76 high-resolution types, and a deconvolution-inferred subset are not matched labels, so 'the SST population' denotes a different entity in each entry.
Two of the cohorts (ROSMAP prefrontal atlas and the 638-individual deconvolution) draw from the same parent study population, so their agreement is not fully independent.
n is not comparable: three entries count donors profiled by snRNA-seq, one counts bulk-profiled individuals with a separate 24-donor reference, and one reports no donor count.
Pathology axes differ (Braak stage, continuous pseudo-progression score, tangle density, amyloid burden), so 'depleted in AD' is anchored to different variables.
Reported quantities are mixed: relative abundance change, loss epoch along a trajectory, vulnerability classification, protein-pathology association and an F statistic.
data_sources.what_it_reveals_from_evidence: Four independent human cohorts of very different size and design (84 multimodal SEA-AD donors, 427 ROSMAP prefrontal donors, 48 donors across six regions, 638 deconvolved bulk profiles) converge on depletion of SST inhibitory neurons in AD, while a fifth analysis shows the signal can vanish when the statistical unit shifts from absolute neuron number to proportion. The comparison separates reproducible direction-of-effect from fragile significance.

figures.what_it_reveals_that_text_cannot: Plotting cohort size against reported outcome, with annotation for shared parent populations and for the reanalysis in which the signal vanishes under a change of statistical unit, separates reproducible direction-of-effect from fragile significance.

subsections.title: The postmortem record: a four-fold range and two outright nulls
subsections.job: Present the 1980s-2020s postmortem series as incommensurable quantities - SST-28-selective neuron density, SST mRNA-expressing cell density, pan-SST immunoreactive counts, bulk peptide concentration - spanning -41% to beyond -70%, with two studies reporting no reduction at all and no number. State that excluding the numberless nulls biases the visible distribution toward loss.

subsections.title: Is the deficit specific to Alzheimer-type pathology?
subsections.job: Use the cross-disease postmortem panel: deficits of 28-58% in AD, Alzheimer-type parkinsonian dementia and olivopontocerebellar atrophy but absent in progressive supranuclear palsy, against the finding of comparable cortical somatostatin reductions in schizophrenia. Conclude that the deficit tracks neither neurodegeneration in general nor Alzheimer pathology exclusively.

subsections.title: Single-nucleus atlases: the strongest claim in the review, and its fragilities
subsections.job: Audit the convergence across 84 SEA-AD donors with four orthogonal assays, 427 ROSMAP donors, 48 donors across six regions, 638 deconvolved bulk profiles - and state the four caveats that matter: cell-type granularity differs so "the SST population" denotes different entities, two cohorts share a parent population, pathology axes differ, and one reanalysis shows the signal can vanish when the statistical unit shifts from absolute number to proportion.

subsections.title: CSF somatostatin: forty years without a discrimination statistic
subsections.job: Assemble the CSF literature as a biomarker evaluation rather than a group-difference narrative: no sensitivity, specificity, AUC or cut-off in any retrieved study; reductions across unrelated diagnoses; medication effects; assay cross-reactivity with SST-28 and cortistatin uncharacterised in all but one study; absolute concentrations in incompatible units; reversibility after shunting; and no longitudinal or prognostic data beyond pre/post-shunt measurements.

subsections.title: Tissue-quality confounds and the limits of the postmortem record
subsections.job: Treat postmortem interval, brain pH, agonal state and RNA integrity as measurable confounds with disputed uniformity across diagnostic groups, and state that no somatostatin-specific degradation curve exists to bound the reported effect sizes.

subsections.title: What the human evidence licenses
subsections.job: State the defensible human claim precisely: proportional depletion of SST-annotated inhibitory neurons in Alzheimer cortex, appearing early, replicated across cohorts of different design; and explicitly not: a diagnostic fluid marker, a demonstrated mechanism of cell death, or a cross-disease human pattern.

opening_constraint: (sec-circuit-consequences) generated predictions about human brain function from model systems; this section assembles the human measurements that can test them, and finds the cellular claim better supported than the fluid one.
closing_constraint: If SST neurons are depleted early in human AD cortex and the peptide system is degraded, intervention should help. (sec-therapeutics) examines whether any intervention aimed at this system has delivered, and what the failures reveal about the causal claim.

evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: No study retrieved in this cluster reports sensitivity, specificity, AUC or a cut-off for CSF somatostatin as a diagnostic test, despite one 1986 report explicitly proposing it as an antemortem diagnostic. The retrieved literature reports only group differences, p-values and correlations.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: A biomarker claim cannot be evaluated, let alone compared with core CSF amyloid and tau markers, without discrimination statistics; the review must not translate 'significantly reduced' into 'diagnostically useful'.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Longitudinal and prognostic CSF somatostatin data
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: No retrieved study follows CSF somatostatin within individuals over time or tests whether baseline CSF somatostatin predicts conversion from mild cognitive impairment to dementia. The only within-subject longitudinal data found are pre- and post-shunt measurements in normal pressure hydrocephalus.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Cross-sectional group differences cannot distinguish a state marker of CSF dynamics from a progressive marker of interneuron loss, and the shunt study shows the measure is reversible.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Assay comparability for CSF and tissue somatostatin
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Only one retrieved study documents an assay that does not cross-react with cortistatin, and only two resolve molecular forms by HPLC. No study retrieved compares radioimmunoassay against mass spectrometry on the same samples, and pre-analytical variables (collection tube, gradient position, freeze-thaw, time to freezing) are not reported.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Four decades of conflicting CSF and tissue somatostatin results may be partly an assay artefact; without cross-assay calibration the discrepancies cannot be attributed to biology.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Primary experimental source for the claim that SST interneurons are the most vulnerable interneuron class in AD
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Primary experimental demonstration with a direct, quantitative within-tissue comparison against parvalbumin and VIP populations in human AD cortex. The claim is repeated across modern single-nucleus papers, which cite one another and earlier peptide studies; the one retrieved study making an explicit SST-versus-parvalbumin comparison is in the Parkinson's disease amygdala and finds the opposite ordering.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Risk of false consensus: a widely stated vulnerability hierarchy whose cross-marker comparison in human AD tissue was not traced to a primary quantitative source in these searches.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Postmortem SST pathology outside Alzheimer's disease
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Quantitative SST cell counts in ALS, frontotemporal lobar degeneration, Huntington's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies cortex. Retrieved non-AD human evidence is limited to CSF measurements in Parkinson's disease, one Parkinson's amygdala co-localisation study, and one negative cortical study that included Parkinson's disease with dementia.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: The cluster's cross-disease claim currently rests on CSF rather than tissue for every disease except AD, so disease-specificity of SST neuron loss is untested at the cellular level.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Reconciliation of cell loss versus peptide and fibre pathology
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: A modern study applying unbiased stereology together with single-nucleus profiling to the same human cases, to test whether SST transcript and peptide reductions reflect actual neuron death or downregulation in surviving neurons.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Two retrieved studies report unchanged SST cell density with dystrophic SST fibres, and one asserts the deficit occurs without major neuron loss, directly contradicting the depletion interpretation that modern single-nucleus compositional analyses place on falling SST abundance.

evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: No retrieved study reports sensitivity, specificity, AUC or a validated cut-off for CSF somatostatin; the one series that addressed discrimination explicitly concluded that distributions overlap controls and multi-infarct dementia so heavily that the measure has no diagnostic specificity
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: The biomarker literature is built on group mean differences only, so the repeated claim that CSF somatostatin is an Alzheimer biomarker has never been tested as a classifier

evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: No cross-calibration between the in-house radioimmunoassays used across cohorts, and only a single small MALDI-MS study (3 AD, 3 FTD, 2 controls) examining whether RIA signal reflects intact peptide rather than processing fragments; peptide half-life itself is altered in Alzheimer cortex
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Reported concentrations differ by unit and by an order of magnitude between laboratories, which blocks meta-analysis and explains why no cut-off has transferred

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Unbiased stereological SST neuron counts in modern postmortem cohorts
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Retrieved human counting studies are immunocytochemical cell-density or fibre-length measurements, several without design-based stereology; the two studies that applied atrophy correction or direct counting found no significant somatostatin neuron loss
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Whether the transcriptomic SST depletion signal corresponds to actual neuron death or to reduced SST expression per surviving neuron cannot be settled from the existing counting literature

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Single-nucleus and spatial atlases outside Alzheimer's disease
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Retrieved single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomic evidence for SST subtype depletion is overwhelmingly Alzheimer-focused; for Parkinson's disease the only comparable human cortical evidence is proteome-based deconvolution, and no equivalent atlas-scale SST subtype analysis was retrieved for progressive supranuclear palsy, multiple system atrophy, Huntington's disease or ALS/FTLD
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Cross-disease specificity of SST subtype vulnerability, which the postmortem RIA literature suggests is restricted to Alzheimer-type pathology, cannot be tested at subtype resolution

unreplicated_claims_to_flag.claim: CSF somatostatin precursor processing is impaired in AD, with lowered SST-14 and a significant increase in the unprocessed 15 kDa prosomatostatin, proposed as an antemortem diagnostic test.
APOE epsilon-4 carriers have roughly 41% lower frontal cortex somatostatin concentration than epsilon-2/3 patients.
Somatostatin gene variant rs4988514 raises AD risk with an odds ratio of 1.42 overall and 2.05 within APOE epsilon-4 carriers.
Low CSF somatostatin in probable AD correlates with slowed spectral EEG measures and temporoparietal neuropsychological dysfunction.
Parvalbumin neurons in the PD amygdala co-aggregate alpha-synuclein ten times more often than somatostatin neurons (68.44% versus 6.98%).
Shunting in normal pressure hydrocephalus restores CSF somatostatin in all patients without improving cognitive performance.

framing_limits: This is the least directly verified literature in the review: 22 of 87 findings were read in full text because the older postmortem and CSF series are closed-access. The synthesis must rest on the modern open-access cohorts, with the historical series treated as an abstract-level record, and the asymmetry stated in the section itself.
No diagnostic accuracy statistic exists for CSF somatostatin in any retrieved study; "significantly reduced" must never be rendered as "diagnostically useful".

certified_evidence_limits.search_coverage: Europe PMC-dominant retrieval. Endpoints actually used: Europe PMC REST search (resultType=core) and fullTextXML, NCBI E-utilities efetch (db=pmc), CrossRef. No other database contributed a comparable share, so coverage claims must be scoped to these sources.
certified_evidence_limits.citation_chasing: None. No backward or forward citation chasing was performed. No section may claim completeness of coverage; write 'no study examining X was retrieved by these searches', never 'no study has examined X'.
certified_evidence_limits.fulltext_shortfall_concentration: The shortfall is concentrated in pre-2000 closed-access postmortem and CSF literature (radioimmunoassay series), which is recorded at abstract level only. Sections whose argument rests on that literature must state the asymmetry in the section body, not only in Methods.
certified_evidence_limits.disconfirming_sweeps: Disconfirming-evidence sweeps were capped per query. Negative-result and conflict coverage is a top-relevance sample, not a census. Report null results as 'reported null results include ...'; never as 'no contradicting evidence exists'. No rate of contradiction may be reported as complete.
certified_evidence_limits.conflict_axis_labels_provisional: Axes were assigned by a documented rule applied to the recorded nature_of_conflict text. Five candidate axes (measurement modality and what was counted; species, region and circuit context; model construct and species transfer; cohort composition, stage and comorbidity; design rigor and statistical unit) were keyword-scored, with the region/species axis down-weighted (0.55) because regional context is named in almost every conflict record, and design rigor up-weighted (1.3) because it is named rarely and only when it is the point. Each conflict carries a primary axis and the full set of axes present, since most of these disagreements are genuinely multi-axis. These tags are a planning classification derived from the conflict text, not a measurement; the writing phase should correct any tag that misreads a conflict, and the atlas figure must state that conflicts can appear in more than one axis row.
certified_evidence_limits.conflict_inventory_caveat: This inventory is the set of disagreements recorded during a search whose disconfirming-evidence sweeps were capped per query. It is a top-relevance sample of the disagreement in this literature, not a census, and no rate of contradiction may be reported as complete.

Claims of the form "no study has examined X" are written as "no study examining X was retrieved by these searches", and every such statement in a body section is sourced to a recorded evidence gap rather than asserted.

scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Every figure specification states the heterogeneity it must display rather than smooth, and the document-level figure rules forbid pooled summaries outright.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_explains_the_discrepancy: Whether cortical SST-immunoreactive cell density is actually reduced in Alzheimer-type dementia. One study reports 60-80% loss of SST28-IR neuron density in cortical areas 9 and 25; the other reports no decrease in neocortical SST-IR cell density versus aged normals, attributing the pathology instead to swollen, plaque-associated SST fibres. The studies differ in antiserum specificity (SST-28-selective versus generic somatostatin), cortical area sampled, and whether density was formally quantified.

Whether cortical somatostatin-like immunoreactivity is reduced in AD at all. The first RIA study reports reduced cortical SLI in AD/SDAT; the later study, matching cases and controls for age and postmortem delay and measuring both SLI and [3H]somatostatin binding in areas 9 and 21, finds no significant change in any disease group and concludes somatostatinergic involvement is not a consistent primary feature.

Method-dependent disagreement on whether the cortical somatostatin deficit reflects loss of somatostatin neurons: tissue radioimmunoassay finds lower SLI in 9 of 10 cortical regions, whereas atrophy-corrected immunocytochemical morphometry in the same disease finds no significant difference in somatostatin-immunoreactive perikaryal number or fibre length. Peptide content per neuron and detectability of lightly stained neurons are the unresolved confounds.

Whether the cortical somatostatin deficit is tied to Alzheimer-type pathology: one postmortem series restricts the ~40% cortical reduction to parkinsonian cases that carry Alzheimer-type cortical pathology, implying pathology-dependence, whereas a schizophrenia-versus-Alzheimer comparison finds comparable cortical somatostatin reductions in schizophrenia, a disorder without Alzheimer-type pathology.

Whether CSF somatostatin differentiates dementia from psychiatric illness: one series finds CSF somatostatin low in both Alzheimer's disease and late-life depression, another finds no significant difference in CSF somatostatin across major depression, mania, anxiety and dementia groups while CRH does separate them. Both are small single-centre radioimmunoassay series with different control groups.

Whether the CSF somatostatin deficit generalises across Alzheimer-type dementia: a 75-patient series reports CSF somatostatin-like immunoreactivity 35% below controls, while a course-stratified series finds no significant CSF somatostatin difference in gradually and very slowly progressing SDAT subgroups, with the deficit confined to rapidly declining cases. Subgroup composition rather than assay appears to drive the difference.
